function: Learns IRS phase shifts and BS transmit power (the action also holds the phase-error matrix) with an improved PPO plus a constraint safety layer to maximize the achievable rate (pp. 6-8).
system: IRS-aided multi-cell NOMA: 5 BSs, 8 single-antenna users each, passive reflecting IRS, 50-300 elements, 200 x 200 m; BS antennas and band not stated (pp. 3, 11, 12).
method: Improved PPO (policy gradient with mirror-descent update) plus a data-experience-driven safety layer mapping constraint-violating actions to feasible ones; reinforcement learning, 30000 training steps (pp. 7-8, 11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rayleigh BS/IRS-to-user links with path loss exponent 3, Rician BS-to-IRS (factor 0.4), averaged over 5000 realizations; random IRS phases (p. 11).
test_conditions: Same network for training and evaluation, rate curves over 30000 training steps; sweeps of distortion coefficients, reflecting elements and power; no test in an unseen scenario (pp. 11-13).
baselines: Learned: SAC, DDPG, A2C, MAB [26] (Fig. 6). Non-learned: SDP relaxation solved with CVX (Table I), random reflection (Fig. 6) (pp. 11-13).
metrics: Communication achievable rate (bps/Hz), utility (bps/Hz per element), policy learning success rate, training loss, FLOPs, rate gain over SDP (pp. 11-13).
complexity: 11 MFLOPs for ANNS, 7.53% of ShuffleNet V2 (146 MFLOPs); no order of complexity or run time given (p. 13).
q1_support: p. 11: "is Rayleigh fading with the path loss exponent 3". Not met: custom Rayleigh and Rician (factor 0.4) simulator with random IRS phases; no 3GPP model, public ray-tracing dataset or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 12: "show the policy learning success rate for reflecting elements 50, 100, 200, 300". Not met: these are training curves per configuration (Figs. 4-7 sweep distortion coefficient, element count and power); the paper never tests a trained model on a configuration unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 11: "we use a comparison with the state-of-the-art deep reinforcement learning algorithms, i.e., Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) [40], Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) [41], Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C) [42]"; p. 13: "ANNS exhibits superior performance compared to SDP" (Table I, achievable rate; SDP solved with CVX); Fig. 6 (p. 12) adds random reflection.
q4_support: p. 13: "ANNS has only 11 MFLOPs, which is only 7.53% of ShuffleNet V2" (number of floating point operations of the proposed model).
q5_support: p. 11: "We find the average channel from 5000 realizations". Not met: the channels come from the authors' own simulator; no code or data link, public dataset or measured data appears in the paper.
notes: Area 3: the learned actions are the IRS phase shifts and the BS power (p. 7: action {Θp(t+1), ΘEl(t+1), Pl(t+1)}); the agent is an improved PPO with a data-experience-driven safety layer (pp. 7-8). q3 counts SAC, DDPG and A2C (standard DRL algorithms applied to the same problem) and MAB [26] as learned baselines, and SDP solved with CVX and random reflection as non-learned baselines, all on the achievable rate. q2 is 0: the CSI-error and residual-phase-noise cases of Fig. 6(b) (p. 13) are impairment sweeps, not new scenarios. The BS antenna number and the carrier band are not stated; p. 3 only says that every mobile device has a single antenna. The paper also derives a closed-form approximate rate under hardware damage (Theorem 1, p. 4) and a convergence proof (Theorem 3, p. 10), which are not the learned method.
